p.src: Now the man who had knocked Dong Zhuo down was none other than Li Ru. Li Ru immediately helped Dong Zhuo to his feet and led him into the study, where he settled him in a seat. Dong Zhuo said, “Why have you come here?” Li Ru replied, “I had just reached the gate of your residence when I learned that Your Excellency had angrily entered the rear garden in search of Lü Bu. I hurried here and met Lü Bu rushing out, crying, ‘The Grand Preceptor means to kill me!’ In alarm, I rushed into the garden to mediate, never imagining that I would accidentally collide with my lord. I deserve death! I deserve death!” Dong Zhuo said, “That intolerable traitor! He trifled with my beloved; I swear I shall kill him!” Li Ru said, “My lord, you are mistaken. At King Zhuang of Chu’s ‘Broken Hat-String’ banquet, he did not investigate Jiang Xiong for molesting his beloved consort; later, when Qin troops surrounded him, Jiang Xiong fought desperately and rescued him. Diao Chan is but one woman, whereas Lü Bu is Your Excellency’s trusted and valiant general. If Your Excellency takes this opportunity to bestow Diao Chan upon Lü Bu, he will be grateful for this great favor and surely repay you with his life. I beg Your Excellency to consider it carefully.” After pondering for a long while, Dong Zhuo said, “There is truth in what you say. I shall consider it.”

p.src: Li Ru thanked him and withdrew. Dong Zhuo entered the rear hall, summoned Diao Chan, and asked, “Why have you been carrying on a secret affair with Lü Bu?” Weeping, Diao Chan replied, “I was admiring the flowers in the rear garden when Lü Bu suddenly appeared. As I drew back in alarm, he said, ‘I am the Grand Preceptor’s son. Why need you avoid me?’ Brandishing his halberd, he pursued me as far as Phoenix Pavilion. Seeing his wicked intent and fearing he would force himself upon me, I tried to throw myself into the lotus pond, but the brute seized me. While I hovered between life and death, Your Excellency arrived and saved me.” Dong Zhuo said, “What if I now bestow you upon Lü Bu?” Diao Chan was horrified and cried, “I have already served Your Excellency, yet now you suddenly mean to give me to a household slave. I would rather die than suffer such disgrace!” She snatched the precious sword from the wall and made to cut her own throat. Dong Zhuo hastily wrested away the sword, embraced her, and said, “I was only teasing you!” Diao Chan collapsed into his arms, covered her face, and sobbed, “This must be Li Ru’s scheme! He is close to Lü Bu and therefore devised this plan; yet he cares nothing for Your Excellency’s dignity or this wretched woman’s life. I would devour his flesh alive!” Dong Zhuo said, “How could I bear to part with you?” Diao Chan said, “Though I am blessed with Your Excellency’s affection, I fear it is unsafe to remain here much longer, for Lü Bu will surely harm me.” Dong Zhuo said, “Tomorrow I shall take you back to Mei Fortress, where we shall enjoy ourselves together. Do not worry or doubt me.” Only then did Diao Chan dry her tears and bow in gratitude. The next day Li Ru came before him and said, “This is an auspicious day. You may send Diao Chan to Lü Bu.” Dong Zhuo said, “Lü Bu and I stand as father and son; it would be improper to bestow her upon him. I shall simply decline to pursue his offense. Convey my wishes and soothe him with kind words.” Li Ru said, “Your Excellency must not let a woman bewitch you.” Dong Zhuo’s expression changed. “Would your wife consent to be given to Lü Bu? Say no more about Diao Chan; one more word and I shall have you beheaded!” Li Ru went out, looked up to heaven, and sighed, “We shall all die at the hands of a woman!” A later reader, reaching this passage, lamented it in verse:

p.src: That very day Dong Zhuo ordered the return to Mei Fortress, and all the officials came to bow and see him off. From her carriage Diao Chan saw Lü Bu at a distance amid the throng, gazing into the carriage. Diao Chan half-covered her face, feigning bitter weeping. When the carriage had gone far away, Lü Bu slackened his reins atop an earthen rise, watched the dust behind it, and sighed in grief and resentment. Suddenly someone behind him asked, “Marquis of Wen, why did you not accompany the Grand Preceptor? Why do you stand here gazing after him and sighing?” Lü Bu looked and saw that it was Minister of the Interior Wang Yun. After they had exchanged greetings, Wang Yun said, “These past days I have been confined at home with a slight illness, so I have not seen you for a long while. Today, as the Grand Preceptor was returning to Mei Fortress, I had no choice but to come out despite my illness to see him off, and happily I have encountered you. May I ask why you are sighing here?” Lü Bu said, “It is all on account of your daughter.” Feigning surprise, Wang Yun said, “Has she still not been given to you after all this time?” Lü Bu said, “That old villain has long kept her for his own pleasure!” Wang Yun feigned utter astonishment. “I cannot believe such a thing!” Lü Bu related to Wang Yun every detail of what had happened. Wang Yun raised his face and stamped his feet, remaining speechless for a long while; at length he said, “I never imagined the Grand Preceptor would commit such a beastly deed!” Then, taking Lü Bu by the hand, he said, “Come to my humble home, and we shall discuss the matter.”

p.src: Lü Bu accompanied Wang Yun home. Wang Yun ushered him into a private chamber and entertained him with wine. Lü Bu once again recounted in detail his encounter at Phoenix Pavilion. Wang Yun said, “The Grand Preceptor has violated my daughter and stolen your wife. Truly, this will make us the laughingstock of the realm—not the Grand Preceptor, but you and me! Yet I am merely an old and feeble man, unworthy of mention; but it is a pity that you, a hero unmatched in all the world, should suffer such humiliation!” Lü Bu’s rage soared to the heavens, and he struck the table with a great shout. Wang Yun hurriedly said, “This old man has spoken amiss. Please calm your anger, General.” Lü Bu said, “I swear I shall kill that old villain and wash away my shame!” Wang Yun hastily covered his mouth. “Do not say such things, General, lest you implicate this old man.” Lü Bu said, “A true man born between heaven and earth—how can he remain forever stifled beneath another?” Wang Yun said, “With your abilities, you are indeed not a man whom Grand Preceptor Dong can hold in check.” Lü Bu said, “I want to kill that old villain, but as we stand in the relation of father and son, I fear what later generations may say.” Wang Yun smiled faintly. “Your surname is Lü, while the Grand Preceptor’s is Dong. When he hurled his halberd at you, where was this bond between father and son?” Lü Bu exclaimed with sudden resolve, “Had the Minister not spoken, I would nearly have ruined myself!” Seeing that his mind was made up, Wang Yun persuaded him further: “If you uphold the House of Han, you will be a loyal minister, your name recorded in the green annals and your honor handed down for a hundred generations; but if you aid Dong Zhuo, you will be a rebel minister, condemned in the histories and leaving a stench for ten thousand years.” Lü Bu left his seat, bowed, and said, “My mind is made up. Have no doubts, Minister.” Wang Yun said, “I fear only that the undertaking may fail and bring disaster upon us instead.” Lü Bu drew the knife at his belt, cut his arm until it bled, and swore an oath. Wang Yun knelt and thanked him. “That the sacrifices of Han shall not be cut off will be entirely due to your grace, General. You must reveal this to no one! When the time comes, I shall devise a plan and inform you.” Lü Bu gave his solemn assent and departed.

p.src: Wang Yun immediately invited Imperial Secretary Shisun Rui and Colonel-Director of Retainers Huang Wan to confer with him. Shisun Rui said, “His Majesty has only just recovered from illness. We can send an eloquent man to Mei Fortress to summon Dong Zhuo for deliberations; meanwhile, give Lü Bu a secret edict from the Emperor and have armored troops lie in ambush within the palace gate, so that Dong Zhuo may be lured inside and put to death. This is the best strategy.” Huang Wan said, “Who would dare undertake the mission?” Shisun Rui said, “Li Su, a Cavalry Commandant from Lü Bu’s home commandery, deeply resents Dong Zhuo for failing to promote him. If we send this man, Dong Zhuo will surely suspect nothing.” Wang Yun said, “Excellent.” They invited Lü Bu to join their deliberations. Lü Bu said, “This is the same man who once persuaded me to kill Ding Jianyang. If he refuses to go now, I shall behead him first.” A messenger was sent to summon Li Su in secret. Lü Bu said, “In former days you persuaded me to kill Ding Jianyang and go over to Dong Zhuo; now Dong Zhuo deceives the Emperor above and cruelly oppresses the people below. His crimes have reached their full measure, and both men and gods are enraged. You can carry an imperial edict to Mei Fortress, summon Dong Zhuo to court, and have concealed troops kill him, thereby lending all your strength to uphold the House of Han so that together we may become loyal ministers. What do you think?” Li Su said, “I too have long wished to rid the world of this villain; I regretted only that I had no like-minded ally. Now that you propose this, General, it is a gift from Heaven. How could I dare harbor a second heart?” He broke an arrow and swore an oath. Wang Yun said, “If you can accomplish this undertaking, why should you fear that high office will not be yours?”

p.src: The next day, Li Su led a dozen horsemen to Mei Citadel. When it was reported that he bore an imperial decree, Dong Zhuo ordered that he be admitted. Li Su entered and bowed. Dong Zhuo asked, “What decree has the Son of Heaven issued?” Li Su replied, “The Son of Heaven has only recently recovered from illness and wishes to assemble the civil and military officials in Weiyang Palace to discuss yielding the throne to the Imperial Preceptor. Hence this decree.” Dong Zhuo asked, “What does Wang Yun think of this?” Li Su replied, “Minister Wang has already ordered men to build an Altar of Abdication. All that remains is for my lord to come.” Overjoyed, Dong Zhuo said, “Last night I dreamed that a dragon enveloped my body, and now this glad news has indeed arrived. The opportunity must not be lost!” He immediately ordered his trusted commanders Li Jue, Guo Si, Zhang Ji, and Fan Chou to guard Mei Citadel with three thousand Flying Bear troops, while he prepared his carriage and returned to the capital that very day. Turning to Li Su, he said, “When I become emperor, I shall make you Commandant of the Capital.” Li Su bowed his thanks and addressed him as sovereign. Dong Zhuo went inside to take leave of his mother. His mother, then over ninety years old, asked, “Where are you going, my son?” Dong Zhuo replied, “Your son is going to receive the abdication of the Han. Before long, Mother, you will be Empress Dowager!” His mother said, “Of late my flesh has trembled and my heart has quailed. I fear it is no auspicious omen.” Dong Zhuo replied, “You are about to become Mother of the Realm. How could there not be signs to startle you beforehand?” He then bade his mother farewell and departed. As he was leaving, he told Diaochan, “When I become Son of Heaven, I shall make you an Imperial Consort.” Diaochan already understood the whole scheme, but feigned delight and bowed her thanks.

p.src: Dong Zhuo left the citadel and mounted his carriage; escorted before and behind, he set out for Chang'an. Before they had gone thirty li, a wheel of his carriage suddenly broke, and Dong Zhuo alighted and mounted a horse. Before they had gone another ten li, the horse reared and neighed, snapping its reins. Dong Zhuo asked Li Su, “The carriage has lost a wheel and the horse has broken its reins. What do these omens mean?” Li Su replied, “They signify that the Imperial Preceptor shall receive the Han abdication, cast off the old for the new, and ride in a jade carriage upon a golden saddle.” Dong Zhuo was pleased and believed him. The next day, while they were on the road, a violent wind suddenly sprang up and a dark mist veiled the sky. Dong Zhuo asked Li Su, “What omen is this?” Li Su replied, “When my lord ascends the dragon throne, crimson radiance and purple mist must appear to magnify Heaven's majesty.” Again Dong Zhuo rejoiced and harbored no suspicion. When he reached the city outskirts, all the officials came out to welcome him. Only Li Ru, confined at home by illness, could not come to greet him. Dong Zhuo proceeded to the chancellor's residence, where Lü Bu came to congratulate him. Dong Zhuo said, “When I ascend the imperial throne, you shall command all the armies under Heaven.” Lü Bu bowed his thanks and lodged that night before Dong Zhuo's tent. That night, a dozen children sang in the countryside, and the wind carried their song into the tent. The song went: “Grass for a thousand li—how green, how green! Above ten days, none may live!” The song sounded mournful and piercing. Dong Zhuo asked Li Su, “What good or ill does this children's rhyme foretell?” Li Su replied, “It merely means that the house of Liu shall fall and the house of Dong shall rise.”

p.src: Early the next morning, Dong Zhuo arrayed his ceremonial escort and entered the court. Suddenly he saw a Daoist in a blue robe and white headcloth, holding a long pole from which hung a bolt of cloth ten feet long, with the character “mouth” written at either end. Dong Zhuo asked Li Su, “What does this Daoist mean by that?” Li Su replied, “He is a man afflicted in the mind.” He called on the soldiers to drive the man away. As Dong Zhuo proceeded toward the court, the officials, each in court robes, greeted him along the road. Li Su walked beside the carriage, a jeweled sword in his hand. At the Northern Side Gate, all the troops were stopped outside; only the twenty-odd attendants of the imperial carriage entered with him. From afar Dong Zhuo saw Wang Yun and the others standing at the palace gate, each holding a jeweled sword. Startled, he asked Li Su, “Why are they carrying swords?” Li Su gave no answer and pushed the carriage straight inside. Wang Yun cried out, “The traitor is here! Where are the warriors?” More than a hundred men sprang out from either side and thrust at him with halberds and spears. Dong Zhuo's armor prevented the weapons from penetrating, but he was wounded in the arm and fell from the carriage. He shouted, “Where is my son Fengxian?” Lü Bu strode out from behind the carriage and thundered, “By imperial decree, I punish the traitor!” With one thrust of his halberd he pierced Dong Zhuo's throat, and Li Su swiftly cut off his head and held it aloft. Holding his halberd in his left hand, Lü Bu drew the decree from his robe with his right and cried, “By imperial decree, I have punished the traitorous minister Dong Zhuo. All others are pardoned!” The officers and soldiers all cried, “Long live the Emperor!” A later poet lamented Dong Zhuo in these lines:

p.src: Now Lü Bu cried aloud, “The man who helped Dong Zhuo perpetrate his cruelties was none other than Li Ru! Who will seize him?” Li Su immediately volunteered to go. Suddenly shouts arose outside the court gate, and word came that Li Ru's own servants had bound him and brought him to surrender. Wang Yun ordered that he be bound, taken to the execution ground in the marketplace, and beheaded. He also had Dong Zhuo's corpse displayed as a warning in the public thoroughfare. Dong Zhuo's corpse was grossly fat. The soldiers guarding it placed a flame in its navel as a lamp, and his grease flowed all over the ground. None of the common people who passed failed to strike his head with their hands or trample his corpse underfoot. Wang Yun then ordered Lü Bu, Huangfu Song, and Li Su to lead fifty thousand troops to Mei Citadel and confiscate Dong Zhuo's property and household.

Wang Yun ordered that he be bound, taken to the execution ground in the marketplace, and beheaded.
He also had Dong Zhuo's corpse displayed as a warning in the public thoroughfare.
Dong Zhuo's corpse was grossly fat. The soldiers guarding it placed a flame in its navel as a lamp, and his grease flowed all over the ground.
None of the common people who passed failed to strike his head with their hands or trample his corpse underfoot.
Wang Yun then ordered Lü Bu, Huangfu Song, and Li Su to lead fifty thousand troops to Mei Citadel and confiscate Dong Zhuo's property and household.

p.src: Now when Li Jue, Guo Si, Zhang Ji, and Fan Chou heard that Dong Zhuo was dead and Lü Bu was approaching, they led the Flying Bear troops away by night and fled to Liangzhou. When Lü Bu reached Mei Citadel, the first person he took away was Diaochan. Huangfu Song ordered that all the sons and daughters of respectable families held in the citadel be released. But every relative of Dong Zhuo, old or young, was put to death. Dong Zhuo's mother was also killed. His younger brother Dong Min and his nephew Dong Huang were both beheaded and their heads publicly displayed. They inventoried and confiscated the hundreds of thousands in gold stored in the citadel, along with countless silks, jewels, vessels, and provisions, and reported back to Wang Yun. Wang Yun richly rewarded the troops, then held a banquet in the main government hall, summoning all the officials to drink in celebration. In the midst of the feast, someone suddenly reported, “Dong Zhuo's corpse lies exposed in the marketplace, and a man has unexpectedly thrown himself over it and is weeping bitterly.” Wang Yun angrily said, “Dong Zhuo has been executed, and every official and commoner celebrates. Who is this man, that he dares to mourn him?” He called to the guards, “Seize him and bring him before me!”

p.src: Presently the man was brought in under arrest. When the assembled officials saw him, they were all astonished: he was none other than Cai Yong, the Palace Attendant. Wang Yun rebuked him, “The traitor Dong Zhuo has been executed today, a great blessing to the realm. You are a minister of Han, yet instead of celebrating for the realm, you mourn a traitor. Why?” Cai Yong acknowledged his guilt and said, “Though I lack ability, I understand the great principles. How could I turn my back on the realm and side with Dong Zhuo? It was only because I remembered how he once recognized my worth that, overcome for a moment, I wept for him. I know that my crime is grave. I beg your lordship's forgiveness. If I might be branded on the forehead and have my feet cut off, yet be allowed to complete the history of Han and thereby atone for my offense, I should count myself fortunate.” The officials valued Cai Yong's talent and all pleaded vigorously for his life. Grand Tutor Ma Midi also privately told Wang Yun, “Bojie is a rare and extraordinary genius. If he were permitted to complete the history of Han, it would truly be a splendid achievement. Moreover, he has long been renowned for filial conduct. If you put him to death so hastily, I fear you will lose the people's esteem.” Wang Yun replied, “In former times, Emperor Wu spared Sima Qian and later allowed him to write history, with the result that a slanderous book was handed down to posterity. Now the fortunes of the realm are in decline and the government is in disorder. We cannot allow a fawning minister to wield his brush beside a young sovereign and expose us all to his censure.” Ma Midi withdrew without another word and privately told the assembled officials, “Will Wang Yun perhaps leave no descendants? Good men are the guiding principle of a nation; its writings and institutions are the canon of a nation. How can one endure after destroying its guiding principle and abolishing its canon?” Wang Yun refused to heed Ma Midi's words and ordered Cai Yong taken to prison and strangled to death. All the scholar-officials who heard the news shed tears for him. Later commentators held that Cai Yong was certainly wrong to mourn Dong Zhuo, but that Wang Yun, in killing Cai Yong, also went far too far. A poem laments:

p.src: Now Li Jue, Guo Si, Zhang Ji, and Fan Chou had fled to Shaanxi, whence they sent a man to Chang'an with a memorial begging pardon. Wang Yun said, “Dong Zhuo's tyranny was aided in every respect by these four men. Though a general amnesty has now been proclaimed throughout the realm, these four alone shall not be pardoned.” The envoy returned and reported this to Li Jue. Li Jue said, “Since our plea for pardon has failed, we may as well each flee for his life.” The strategist Jia Xu said, “If you gentlemen abandon your troops and travel alone, even the head of a mere post station could bind you. Better to rally the people of Shaanxi and your own troops, storm into Chang'an, and avenge Dong Zhuo. If the enterprise succeeds, uphold the court and bring order to the realm; if it fails, it will still not be too late to flee.” Li Jue and the others approved his counsel and spread a rumor throughout Xiliang: “Wang Yun intends to exterminate everyone from this region.” Everyone was stricken with alarm. Then they proclaimed again, “There is no profit in dying for nothing. Will you follow us in revolt?” All declared themselves willing to follow. Thus they gathered more than a hundred thousand men, divided them into four columns, and drove toward Chang'an. On the road they met Dong Zhuo's son-in-law, General of the Household Niu Fu, who was leading five thousand troops to avenge his father-in-law. Li Jue joined forces with him, made him the vanguard, and the four leaders advanced one after another.

p.src: When Wang Yun learned that the Xiliang troops were approaching, he consulted Lü Bu. Lü Bu said, “Set your mind at ease, Minister over the Masses. Such vermin are scarcely worth counting!” He then led Li Su and their troops out to meet the enemy. Li Su went first into battle, encountered Niu Fu, and fought a fierce engagement. Niu Fu could not withstand him and fled in defeat. Unexpectedly, during the second watch that night, Niu Fu took advantage of Li Su's unpreparedness and raided his camp. Li Su's troops scattered in confusion. He fled more than thirty li, losing over half his army, and came before Lü Bu. Lü Bu flew into a rage and said, “How dare you blunt the keen edge of my army!” He had Li Su beheaded and hung his head at the camp gate.

p.src: The next day, Lü Bu advanced to engage Niu Fu. How could Niu Fu withstand Lü Bu? Once again he was soundly defeated and fled. That night Niu Fu summoned his confidant Hu Chier and said, “Lü Bu is so fierce and valiant that we can never overcome him. Better to keep Li Jue and the other three in the dark, secretly pack up our gold and pearls, and desert the army with three or five trusted attendants.” Hu Chier agreed. That night they gathered up the treasure and abandoned the camp, with only three or four men accompanying them. As they were about to cross a river, Hu Chier coveted the treasure and murdered Niu Fu, then carried his head to present to Lü Bu. Lü Bu questioned him about the circumstances, whereupon one of the attendants denounced him: “Hu Chier murdered Niu Fu to seize his gold and treasure.” Enraged, Lü Bu immediately had Hu Chier executed. He led his army onward and met Li Jue's forces head-on. Without waiting for them to form ranks, Lü Bu leveled his halberd, spurred his horse forward, and waved his army straight into the attack. Li Jue's army could not withstand the assault and retreated more than fifty li. They encamped below a mountain, and Li Jue summoned Guo Si, Zhang Ji, and Fan Chou to confer. He said, “Though Lü Bu is brave, he lacks strategy and need not concern us. I shall lead troops to hold the mouth of the valley and lure him into combat each day. General Guo can lead a force around to strike his rear, following Peng Yue's method of harrying Chu: advance when the gong sounds and withdraw when the drums roll. Lords Zhang and Fan shall divide their troops into two columns and make straight for Chang'an. Unable to aid both front and rear, he is certain to suffer a crushing defeat.” They all adopted his plan.

p.src: Meanwhile, Lü Bu drew up his troops below the mountain, and Li Jue led his army out to challenge him. Lü Bu charged furiously, and Li Jue retreated up the mountain. Arrows and stones rained down from above, and Lü Bu's troops could advance no farther. Suddenly a report came that Guo Si was attacking from the rear, and Lü Bu hastened back to meet him. But he heard a tremendous rolling of drums, and Guo Si's army had already withdrawn. Just as Lü Bu was about to recall his troops, a gong sounded and Li Jue's army came again. Before he could engage them, Guo Si once more led troops against his rear. By the time Lü Bu arrived, the drums had sounded again and they had withdrawn, provoking him to such fury that his breast nearly burst. This continued for several days: he could neither obtain battle nor break it off. While he was still fuming, a galloping messenger suddenly arrived to report that the two armies under Zhang Ji and Fan Chou had attacked Chang'an itself and the capital was in grave peril. Lü Bu hurriedly led his army back, while Li Jue and Guo Si attacked from behind. Lü Bu had no heart to prolong the fight and thought only of escape, losing many soldiers and horses. By the time he reached the walls of Chang'an, rebel troops had massed like clouds and gathered like rain, completely encircling the city. Lü Bu's army fought them but gained no advantage. The soldiers feared Lü Bu's savage severity, and many surrendered to the rebels, causing him great anxiety.

p.src: Several days later, Dong Zhuo's surviving partisans Li Meng and Wang Fang acted as agents within the city, secretly opened the gates, and the four rebel armies surged in together. Lü Bu charged left and right but could not hold them back. Leading several hundred horsemen beyond the Qingsuo Gate, he called to Wang Yun, “The situation is desperate! Please mount, Minister, and leave the passes with me, that we may devise some better plan elsewhere.” Wang Yun said, “If through the blessing of the spirits of the state I can restore peace to the realm, that is my dearest wish; but if that is not to be, then I shall offer up my life in death. To seek ignoble escape when disaster comes is something I will never do. Convey my respects to the lords east of the passes, and urge them to devote themselves to the welfare of the state!” Lü Bu urged him again and again, but Wang Yun steadfastly refused to leave. Before long flames from every gate leapt to the sky. Lü Bu had no choice but to abandon his family, lead more than a hundred horsemen racing through the pass, and seek refuge with Yuan Shu.

p.src: Li Jue and Guo Si loosed their troops to plunder without restraint. The Minister of Ceremonies Zhong Fu, the Grand Coachman Lu Kui, the Minister Herald Zhou Huan, the Colonel of the City Gates Cui Lie, and the Colonel of the Yue Cavalry Wang Qi all died in the national calamity. The rebel troops pressed the inner court ever more tightly, and the attendants begged the Emperor to ascend the Xuanping Gate and quell the disorder. When Li Jue and the others saw the imperial yellow canopy, they restrained their soldiers and cried, “Long live the Emperor!” Emperor Xian leaned from the tower and asked, “Why have you entered Chang'an without awaiting imperial leave or presenting a memorial? What do you intend?” Li Jue and Guo Si raised their faces and replied, “Grand Preceptor Dong was a minister who upheld Your Majesty and the state, yet Wang Yun murdered him without cause. We have come solely to avenge him and would not dare rebel. Once we see Wang Yun, we shall withdraw our troops.” Wang Yun was then beside the Emperor. Hearing these words, he memorialized, “All I did was planned for the sake of the state. Now that matters have come to this, Your Majesty must not cherish my life and thereby imperil the realm. I beg leave to descend and meet the two rebels.” The Emperor paced to and fro, unable to bring himself to consent. Wang Yun himself leapt down from the tower of the Xuanping Gate and cried aloud, “Wang Yun is here!” Li Jue and Guo Si drew their swords and shouted, “What crime had Grand Preceptor Dong committed that he should be killed?” Wang Yun replied, “The traitor Dong's crimes filled heaven and spanned the earth; they are too many to recount. On the day he was executed, every gentleman and commoner in Chang'an congratulated one another. Can it be that you alone did not hear?” Li Jue and Guo Si said, “The Grand Preceptor may have been guilty; but what crimes had we committed that you refused to pardon us?” Wang Yun cursed them loudly: “Rebel traitors, what need is there for further words? For me, Wang Yun, there is only death today!” The two rebels struck and killed Wang Yun beneath the tower. A court historian composed a poem in his praise:
